sections.html:
Milford is a coastal city in New Haven County, between New Haven and Bridgeport. The 2020 census counted 50,558 residents in about 25 square miles, more than 3 of them water. More than 14 miles of its shoreline face Long Island Sound, and the population has stayed near 50,000 for decades, so most of the housing is mature. Roofs, boilers and sewer laterals are common repair conversations.

Interstate 95 and U.S. Route 1 cross the south of the city, the Wilbur Cross Parkway crosses the north, and the Metro-North New Haven Line stops at Milford station. Many buyers shop by school attendance zone, so a seller should be ready to say which schools serve the address. Five lifeguarded public beaches, Silver Sands State Park and seven private beaches put many homes near salt air and tidal water. Ask your insurer or the city about flood zone status for your lot.

Most of Milford is taxed by the city alone, but a few communities have their own taxing power. The Borough of Woodmont, incorporated in 1903, is chartered by the General Assembly as a municipality yet remains part of the city. Several beach associations were chartered by special act and given powers that include taxing authority:

  • Morningside
  • Point Beach
  • Bayview
  • Walnut Beach
  • Wildermere Beach
  • Laurel Beach

The Tax Collector's page has a link titled Boroughs / Associations. If your home is in Woodmont or one of these beach areas, ask the Tax Collector whether a separate borough or association charge appears alongside the city bill, and have your attorney check it before closing.

One office bills and collects real estate tax, motor vehicle tax, personal property tax, sewer use fees, sewer assessments and sewer laterals. The Assessor's Office certifies the Grand List each October 1, and collection follows that list. The city says it cannot override or make decisions contrary to the Connecticut statutes.

The Board of Aldermen sets the mill rate through the adopted budget, and the Sewer Commission sets the sewer use fee. Call the office or read your bill for installment dates; the Tax Collector's page has the rest.

Because the same office collects sewer charges, a sewer balance can appear in the same payoff request as the real estate tax. The Tax Collector's page lists a sewer use fee history and links for sewer assessments and sewer laterals. Ask for these in writing before closing:

  • The balance on each real estate installment
  • Any unpaid sewer use fee
  • Any open sewer assessment or lateral charge
  • Whether a borough or beach association bill applies to the lot

Owners who have fallen behind may also see the Tax Collector's legal notices of taxes due and an alias tax warrant, both listed on the same page. The office also lists an Emergency Mortgage Assistance Program link.

sections.h2: Who sets the rate and who reviews land use?
sections.html: Milford has a mayor and a 15-member Board of Aldermen, three from each of five districts. The Aldermen adopt the budget that sets the mill rate, and the mayor has no veto over what they pass. A ten-member Planning and Zoning Board handles land use. If you plan to add a unit, convert a garage or split a lot before selling, zoning approval comes from that board, and buyers often ask whether past work was permitted. Pull your permit records before you list.

A Milford payoff request is more than a tax number. Because one office handles real estate, sewer and in some cases collection, build your request around everything it bills. Start by writing down the address and the tax account number from your bill. Then ask the office for the balance on each real estate installment, the status of any sewer use fee, assessment or lateral charge, and whether the account has been sent to its collection agency. If it has, ask who to pay and whether the figure changes.

Give the written results to your closing attorney or title company. They will confirm the numbers against their own search and plan the settlement around them. If your closing date shifts, ask for a fresh figure, since the balance can change.

Before listing, collect permits for anything you have added or converted. A finished attic, an extra unit or a garage turned into living space needs to match what the city has approved, and buyers or their lenders will ask. The Planning and Zoning Board decides land use, so questions about whether a change was allowed belong there. If something was done without approval, talk with your attorney about whether to correct it first or sell as-is and disclose it.

sections.h2: Selling a house in Woodmont or a beach community
sections.html: If your house is in Woodmont or one of the chartered beach areas, you could owe a charge beyond the city bill. That is an extra line for the title company to check. Ask the Tax Collector what applies to your address, write down the answer, and make sure your attorney has it before the closing date is set. Waterfront streets also bring flood zone and insurance questions, so ask your insurer for the zone and the premium history before a buyer asks you.

sections.h2: If you want to sell fast with tax owed
sections.html:
Start with the Tax Collector's payoff figure, because every other choice depends on it. Then compare three paths: pay the arrears and list the house, sell as-is to a cash buyer, or ask the office about a payment arrangement.

An as-is sale lets the title company pay the tax, sewer and other charges out of the proceeds, and it also lets you skip repairs you may not want to fund. Listing takes more time and more spending up front, so weigh each path against how soon you need to close.

faqs.q: Who collects property tax in Milford, CT?
faqs.a: The Milford Tax Collector, at 70 West River Street, First Floor, Room 105. Call 203-783-3217; the office is open Monday through Friday, 8:30 AM to 4:30 PM, except holidays.

faqs.q: What date is the Milford Grand List?
faqs.a: October 1 of each year. The Assessor certifies the list and the Tax Collector bills from it.

faqs.q: Does Milford collect sewer fees with property tax?
faqs.a: The Tax Collector's office collects sewer use fees, sewer assessments and sewer laterals, so ask for those balances along with the tax payoff.

faqs.q: What is the Borough of Woodmont?
faqs.a: It is a borough chartered by the General Assembly with municipal powers, and it still sits within the City of Milford. Ask the Tax Collector how it affects a bill for your address.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Milford house with unpaid taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The unpaid balance is normally paid from sale proceeds at closing, so request a written payoff first.
